external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Providing food at community and charity events
external_sources.supports: Safe preparation, storage and service need planning. Keep current ingredient and allergen information available. A school event proposal is not approval to serve food.

external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Allergen information for non-prepacked foods best practice
external_sources.supports: Use accurate current written information supported by a conversation. Communicate a customer requirement to the responsible trained adult. Never guess or promise that an unchecked item is safe.

evidence.description: Individual portfolio review with two traceable evidence references, a genuine audience question and learner reply, final evidence checklist, next-step statement and actual banking status.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: point and use a sentence frame.
routes.Independent: Independent: explain skill, evidence and help.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: compare progress and a remaining limit.

cases.text: You choose two records with clear work references.
cases.fact: The audience can find the work.
cases.next_step: Explain the task and your action for each.

cases.text: The audience asks what help you used.
cases.fact: Support is part of the evidence context.
cases.next_step: Explain the actual prompt or practical help.
cases.staff_note: Record the genuine question and reply.

cases.fact: A pause can support a clear response.
cases.next_step: Use notes, pointing, writing or usual AAC.
cases.staff_note: Do not answer the assessed question for the learner.

cases.text: One item still needs a staff check.
cases.fact: It is not yet ready to bank as verified.
cases.next_step: Record the check and who will follow it up.
cases.staff_note: Do not mark E before actual storage of checked evidence.

cases.text: You agree a target to read back the full order.
cases.fact: The target names an observable action.
cases.next_step: State the support and a future practice opportunity.

cases.text: Only some items have been checked and stored.
cases.next_step: Record stored references and remaining gaps.
cases.staff_note: Do not claim the whole award is complete.

The source assessment is retained. This lesson contributes evidence; it does not by itself complete an award. Public award labels are masked only.
Purpose and success checks
The weekly scheme line above is shared across two lessons. This lesson focuses on explaining progress and next steps.
How can I explain my progress using my own evidence?
I can explain two pieces of my own work. I can respond to a question or feedback. I can agree a next step and bank checked work.

VOC-W7-L2-E1: Individual portfolio review with two traceable evidence references, a genuine audience question and learner reply, final evidence checklist, next-step statement and actual banking status.
Before pupils arrive

Bring the Lesson 1 index and two authentic records selected by each learner. Agree a quiet adult audience and the learner’s preferred mode. Have approved evidence storage available to staff. No external assessor, employer, visitor or placement is assumed.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.
Calendar and continuity

Monday 14–Friday 18 December 2026. Two 40-minute lessons this week. No teaching day or clock slot is inferred. Any visitor, placement or external audience is unconfirmed; the in-class route is ready to use.
Staff enter the actual teaching date above. Continue the accepted prior-week evidence and support routines.

Access and practice
Supported: point and use a sentence frame. Independent: explain skill, evidence and help. Aspire: compare progress and a remaining limit.

The learner explains two records with task, skill, action and support. An adult asks one genuine question, then records the learner’s own reply. Use NS+ feedback and a response in the learner’s own colour before R. Staff bank only verified items, record actual storage/status, and leave remaining gaps with a next-step statement.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

A quiet one-to-one review, writing, pointing or AAC is acceptable. No public presentation or personal disclosure is required. Keep private records in approved staff storage. Do not invent audience feedback, dates or completion.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. Use the familiar adult as the review audience and available in-class evidence. Record any missing external encounter as missing; do not write a fictional visitor response.
Assessment and feedback

Two records are traceable to this learner and are described accurately. The real audience question and learner response are retained. The next step is specific and includes support. E is used only for evidence actually stored. An unresolved gap stays explicit; this lesson does not certify an award or registration.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Do not require public speaking.
Card B: Record the genuine question and reply.
Card C: Do not answer the assessed question for the learner.
Card D: Do not mark E before actual storage of checked evidence.
Card E: No future date is invented.
Card F: Do not claim the whole award is complete.
Common misunderstandings
Speaking confidently does not replace evidence. Banking some checked work does not mean every requirement is complete. A next-step statement should describe an action, not just “try harder”.
Teaching boundary

A quiet one-to-one review, writing, pointing or AAC is acceptable. No public presentation or personal disclosure is required. Keep private records in approved staff storage. Do not invent audience feedback, dates or completion.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
Assessment boundary
VOC-W7-L2-E1 contributes to the source assessment. No criterion, registration or award completion is invented. Sources: FACTS_LEDGER.md.
